title: Econ Autotune Playbook for Latency-Sensitive Workloads
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Goal: Deliver an operational playbook and lightweight control-plane that automatically recommends and, where safe, applies per-route autotuning knobs (batch size, prefix/KV cache TTL, quantization profile) for latency-sensitive production routes. The playbook covers hypothesis-driven experiments, rollout gating, rollback criteria, and a small telemetry surface for monitoring quality regressions.

Why this ticket: We repeatedly see manual tuning of knobs for a handful of customer routes driving measurable cost savings but inconsistent latency regressions. An autotune approach standardizes experiments, captures workload signals, and automates low-risk adjustments to meet SLOs while lowering unit costs.

Scope: Pilot a non-invasive "suggest-and-audit" autotune for 6 production routes (internal + 3 customers) to evaluate model/quant/latency trade-offs. Deliverables: 1) Playbook doc with experiment matrix and gating; 2) Autotune service prototype (read-only suggestions + UI); 3) Metric dashboards & alerting recipes; 4) Runbook for ops and rollback.

Out of scope: fully automated write-path changes for customer-facing routes (this will be a follow-up if pilot shows low risk).

Notes on approach: Use offline replay from sampled traffic plus live canary windows. Score suggestions by composite econ score = delta_cost_per_request / max(1, delta_p99_latency_ms^2) weighted by traffic volume and customer tier. Prioritize suggestions that reduce cost >=8% with latency impact <=2% p99 for tier-1 internal routes.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc reviewed and approved by Eng, SRE, and PM
Autotune service returns ranked suggestions for knobs for 6 pilot routes
Observed pilot results: >=8% median cost reduction across pilot routes with p99 latency regression <=2% for 4/6 routes
Dashboards show signal-to-noise for quality metrics with alerting thresholds documented
Ops runbook defined with clear rollback steps for each knob type
milestones: 2026-01-28: Data collection and offline replay harness ready
2026-02-15: Internal route pilot begin (observability + canary windows)
2026-03-10: Consolidated results + decision on write-path automation
metrics: unit_cost_delta_percent: relative change in per-request GPU cost
p99_latency_delta_ms: change in 99th percentile latency for the route
suggestion_precision: fraction of suggestions with no adverse quality signal after 24h
time_to_recommend_seconds: latency from ingestion to suggestion generation
manual_override_rate: fraction of suggestions rejected by SRE/PM
risks: Quality regressions that are not visible in our eval sets but surface in production
Insufficient signal in low-traffic routes to make confident recommendations
Cross-dependency between knobs (e.g., aggressive quant + large batch) causing nonlinear regressions
Operational complexity if suggestions are applied automatically without human-in-the-loop
